# Guide for Searching and Troubleshooting Fire Safety Check-Ins

1. Start with inspection records located in both physical and electronic formats.

3. Check for repairs needed, including installation of smoke detectors, sprinkler systems, and other fire safety features as required by local regulations.

5. Once repairs have been completed, schedule a follow up inspection to verify that all repairs were made correctly and are functioning properly.
6. Document the results of each inspection into a secure digital format such as PDF or spreadsheet so you can easily access them later if needed.
7. Utilize a system of reminders (such as automated emails) to help ensure follow up inspections are conducted promptly after repairs are complete.
8. Before entering into future lease agreements

### Accurate Descriptions of All Components and Subsystems

Maintain records of all hardware and software components, any interfaces they may have, dependencies between systems, and any modifications made to the default configurations. These descriptions should include manufacturer information, model numbers, serial numbers, o/s versions, configuration settings, as well as date of installation and date of last update.

### Ensure Easy Accessibility by All Users

### Backup Frequently
